title: Elazığ–Sivrice earthquake of 2020
summary: An Mw 6.8 earthquake struck eastern Turkey on 24 January 2020, caused by strike-slip faulting between the Arabian and Anatolian plates. Studies place its rupture on a roughly 50 km long fault plane, with maximum slip of about 1.9 m.

as_recorded.value: The 24 January 2020 M w  6.7 earthquake in eastern Turkey

where.modern_name: Sivrice, Elazığ, eastern Turkey (East Anatolian Fault Zone)
where.historical_name: Sivrice, Elazığ, eastern Turkey (East Anatolian Fault Zone)

importance.justification: A damaging regional earthquake on the East Anatolian Fault, widely studied, but with limited global historical reach.

sources.title: Source Process of the 24 January 2020 Mw 6.7 East Anatolian Fault Zone, Turkey, Earthquake | Seismological Research Letters | GeoScienceWorld

reviewer_note: Sources give magnitude as Mw 6.8 (ISC GCMT) or 6.7 (the SRL abstract), and other cited titles use 6.75 or 6.7. The sources are scholarly bibliographies and an abstract, so they give no casualty or damage figures, which the summary leaves out. Epicentre coordinates are 38.30, 39.15 per ISC.} (Drafted by the Wikipedia pipeline from isc.ac.uk, pubs.geoscienceworld.org; quotes machine-checked.)
